## About

I am a PhD student in Biostatistics at the **University of Arizona**, working at the intersection of algorithmic fairness, missing data methods, and public health data science. Before Arizona, I earned an MS in Statistics from **Western Michigan University** and a BSc in Mathematics from the University of Mines and Technology (Ghana), and spent several years as a survey statistician with the **Ghana Statistical Service**, working on national census and health-survey projects.

My current research develops game-theoretic frameworks for detecting hidden subgroup bias in clinical prediction models. Alongside that, I work with Africa CDC on public health emergency management capacity building, and with the **Arizona Department of Health Services** on HIV surveillance data infrastructure.

## Research Interests

- **Algorithmic fairness** in clinical AI and prediction models
- **Missing data** — multiple imputation, MNAR sensitivity analysis, tipping-point frameworks
- **Survival analysis** and nonparametric methods
- **Bayesian nonparametrics & network models** — Gaussian process priors, ERGM mixture models, epidemic modeling
- **Global child & maternal health** — anemia and nutrition in Sub-Saharan Africa
- **Public health emergency management** capacity building in Africa
